4.2 made

What happened, how I proved it, the fix I prototyped, and the checklist that keeps it from shipping again.
Built from CLAUDE.md and six modules of my own prompts · data 29 Jun – 6 Sep · prepared 16 Oct 2026
What happened, plainly

Two changes shipped together.
One quietly broke the loop.

60sPing wait cut from 90s. Slow answers became misses.

The headline acceptance number recovered. That hid it, because the four had left the average.

Missed pings stepped up on release day: ~5% on 11 Aug, 28% on 12 Aug, 48% on 13 Aug. Turn-downs stayed flat. Callouts dipped 9–21%, so August being quiet explains only a small part.
Module 1 · Origin Story

Map the system, then see the split.

Could you make a diagram showing me how the nodes in this communication system connect (dispatch to superheroes, etc.) and show all the specific superheroes with their ping rates and acceptance rates, etc.
16 responders, 15 handlers. Acceptance fell 76.6% to 64.0% around 12 Aug while pings per week stayed flat (~172 to ~165). Four responders collapsed from ~48 to ~15 pings a week; the other 12 got busier.
Why it mattered

A flat total with a falling rate is the first sign that someone is being left out. This prompt asked for every responder, not the average, and that is where the four showed up.

Module 2 · Super Hearing

Interviews and tickets disagree.

You've now read both folders. Where do they disagree? What's loud in the interviews but rare in the tickets, and what's all over the tickets that nobody brought up in the interviews?
32 "phone hasn't gone off in N days" tickets, 0 before 4.2, and not one interview mentioned them. Aunt Dot and Kip, whose responders collapsed, filed zero tickets, so tickets undercount the damage.

Module 3 · Rewind

I pushed back on the framing, and the chart showed it.

Okay, I understand the people related to the issue. My hypothesis remains that the folks who are missing the pings are not bad at their jobs, but that there might be something wrong with the technology or their expectations. Can you tell me more about the specific pings that were missed. What qualities do they share compared to pings that were picked up?
The drop is misses, not refusals: ~2% to ~18% missed, turn-downs flat at ~18–21%. The next ping follows a missed one ~61s later, which fits the 60s wait.

Module 3 · Rewind · one responder

The Undertow: 12 pings a week to 1.

Let's go with The Undertow. Show me every week for them, how many times we pinged them, how many they took. Then tell me what happened to that person, week by week, in plain English.
14 pings since 12 Aug: 3 taken, 8 missed. Last yes on 17 Aug, then five straight misses in their home area. Before 4.2 they were pinged for nearly every Harborside callout; after, 9 of 32.

Module 4 · X-Ray Vision

Read the code. Find the penalty.

Find me the part of this code that takes points off somebody when they miss a ping or turn one down. Show it to me and explain it in plain English. Then find me every single thing in this code that puts points back on.
Yes +0.08, no or missed −0.12 (identical), score 0 to 1, starts at 0.5, and it never decays. Break-even is a 60% yes rate. From 0, a responder needs seven straight yeses to reach 0.5.
When you say "that points at the 60-second wait", you are sort of ignoring the fact that the four low responders are getting no pings.
Screenshot · responder-scores-over-time.html (a model of the code, not a measurement)
Module 4 · the question that changed the answer

What the code isn't doing.

If I'd only asked what the code does, not what it doesn't do, what would I have missed?
For a quiet responder, the code has:
No easing back to 0.52019 TODO
No way to earn points without being pingedmissing
No miss vs. refusal splitmissing
No retry, no alert when someone goes quietmissing
The score is the likeliest reason for the quiet, and the 60s wait explains the misses. The routing code also never uses home area; "home vs. outside" was my own join of the data. Open: are misses push failures, and do scores reset on deploy?

Looking good. This is not a silent update from 60 -> 90 seconds, this is highly visible, isn't it? I also like the panel for the "Quiet for a week" scenario... Should we have an interaction that allows them to check, "Am I connected?" Also, I need to make sure our responders have notifications turned on.
"Am I connected?" checks the phone is online and reaching Rook, that the responder is available, and that notifications are on. Notifications being off would look exactly like "my phone never goes off". Untested as a cause.

Module 5 · discipline

I said "later" to the shiny ideas.

What if we had a competitive bidding system, where the top 2-3 responders (based on the already established rankings) are all given the ping at the same time, and they can see that they are competing against other responders?
Parked on purpose. It would hide whether the 4.3 fixes worked, shut out low-ranked responders like The Undertow, and break acceptance rate as a metric. Parked in the brief for Q4.
Reverted

The "selfie with the victim" idea came out of the prototype. It needs victim consent, responder choice, a Security Policy 4.1 review and Legal first. It lives in the brief as a follow-up concept.

Best first experiment from the parked list: a one-tap "why did you miss?" prompt, because it answers the thing we can't see today.
Module 6 · Sidekicks · how it doesn't happen again

A five-point check, every Monday.

Schedule review-checklist to run every Monday morning, and let me know what it finds. Nothing needs to be ready for it to fire today. I'm setting the habit, not waiting on the result.
The skill checks owner, success measures, scope start vs. end, problem before solution, and business value, in the same order every time. 4.2 shows why: Availability Confidence was committed for 4.2 and never shipped or announced, and the ping wait cut was not flagged as a risk. Scope drift and missing value are what this check is built to catch.
